background: Raiffeisen Bank International is the central institution of the Austrian Raiffeisen cooperative banks and a leading lender across Central and Eastern Europe, with a large and long-running exposure to Russia that it has been unable to fully exit.
synthesis: S&P rates the bank A- on positive outlook and Moody's A1 after its upgrade on 11 Jul 2023, stable. Capital is strong against EU and Nordic banks, with CET1 of 17.3% above the peer median and leverage of 8.5% in the top quarter, and so is liquidity, with LCR of 151% just above the median and NSFR of 139% in the top quarter, though LCR has fallen 31 points since 30 Jun 2025. The weak spot is Russia: the newest flagged items, on 17 Sep 2026, are a short seller's claims that it helped Russia circumvent sanctions, which sent the shares sharply lower. That is a sanctions and reputational risk the ratios do not capture.
